title: IS17_interface2_5

lines.explanation: Declares an interface called Shape.
area method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
volume method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
Cube class is extended with the Shape interface. Use the keyword "implements" to implement an interface.
Creates a width object of type integer whose value is set to "2".
Creates a length object of type integer whose value is set to "3".
Creates a height object of type integer whose value is set to "10".
area method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
The area method returns the product of the width and length objects.
volume method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
The volume method returns the product of the width, length, and height objects.
Circle class is extended with the Shape interface. Use the keyword "implements" to implement an interface.
Creates a radius object of type integer whose value is set to "10".
area method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
The area method returns the product of Pi, and the radius squared. PI can be called from the Math object to get the value of Pi.
volume method is declared as public and expected to return an object of type double.
The volume method returns the number "0".

lines.code: Shape[] s = { new Cube(), new Circle() };
lines.explanation: Creates an array for the Shape interface that will hold each Cube and Circle in s.
A For loop that will run until the integer i is no longer less than the length of s, and i will increment by 1 after each iteration.

lines.code: System.out.println("The area and volume of " + s[i].getClass() " is " + s[i].area() + " , " + s[i].volume());
lines.explanation: For the Cube object and the Circle object, the system will print out the class name of each and the area and volume of each.
